problem: Image-goal visual navigation methods rely on odometry, RL trained for tens of millions of steps in simulator, topological graphs, or metric maps, which makes them heavy, data-hungry and dependent on privileged sensing.
motivation: Humans navigate with approximate cognitive maps built from visual cues rather than detailed metric maps. A lightweight agent with no odometry, RL or graph, trained from human point-click demonstrations, would be cheaper and more interpretable, and would also allow easy human-in-the-loop correction.
key_idea: A feudal hierarchy of a memory proxy map (contrastive latent-space visit density), a waypoint-predicting mid-level manager imitating human point-clicks, and a low-level action classifier gives image-goal navigation without odometry, RL or graphs.
insight: Memory organized purely by visual-similarity in a learned latent space is a sufficient replacement for graphs or metric maps: adding the MPM to the ablation raises success by roughly 25% (e.g. Straight avg Succ 37.51 to 57.91 with the RGBD Det variant), and SMoG features track ground-truth distance better than MoCo, SwAV or ResNet. Learned low-level worker beats deterministic waypoint-to-action mapping (about 10%). Human-like waypoint imitation transfers zero-shot from ~37K frames, and editing the MPM lets a human steer exploration.
method: High-level manager / Memory Proxy Map (MPM): images embedded by SMoG contrastive model whose positive pairs come from SuperGlue-based visual clusters; an MLP imitating Isomap projects the 128-d features to 2D, and a Gaussian window (sigma=1) per observation builds a local visit-density map
Mid-level manager WayNet: ResNet-18 modified to 7-channel input (RGBD + MPM crop) trained by supervised imitation of LAVN human point-click waypoints
Goal-directed override: SuperGlue keypoint matching between current view and goal image; if confidence (0.7) is high, mean of matched keypoints replaces the WayNet waypoint
Low-level worker: 4-layer MLP with PReLU taking depth map and waypoint, predicting turn-left 15° / turn-right 15° / forward 0.25 m, trained on human actions
Stop criterion: goal-match confidence high and depth <=1 m, or matched keypoint area ratio psi >= 0.85

Human feedback: a landmark graph is created from MPM clusters; the human marks 'toward' (remove MPM points) or 'away' (fill MPM) to control exploration, and failed episodes are rerun with intervention

setting.backbone: ResNet-18 WayNet + SMoG contrastive encoder + MLP worker + SuperGlue (trained from LAVN data, no RL)
setting.training_data: 117 LAVN human navigation trajectories (36,834 frames, ~37K images); ~3M training iterations total
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (480x640, 120° FoV), goal image, no odometry
setting.action_space: low-level: turn left 15°, turn right 15°, forward 0.25 m
setting.privileged: none for the main method (human-feedback landmark graph uses simulator noise-free actions to estimate agent location)

numbers_note: Benchmark label Gibson-ImageNav used for the NRNS-style Gibson image-goal task; per-difficulty numbers omitted for brevity.
results: On NRNS-protocol Gibson image-goal navigation, FeudalNav reaches 67.5/55.5 (Succ/SPL) on straight and 60.2/39.1 on curved trajectories, beating NRNS+SLING (64.4/50.8; 43.7/14.3) and OVRL+SLING (58.2/42.5; 55.4/37.4) without RL, odometry or graphs. With human feedback on failure cases it reaches 80.78 Succ, above VGM's 76.1, though VGM keeps higher SPL.
limitations: Human-feedback results rerun only failure cases and rely on simulator noise-free actions for landmark positions; SPL gains are small since interventions lengthen paths
Evaluated only in Habitat/Gibson simulation, no real robot; unstable variants with 3-frame history show sensitivity
Depends on SuperGlue matching and a hand-tuned thresholds; inherits biases from human data (e.g. turn preferences)
